source.document: TB MED 507, Heat Stress Control and Heat Casualty Management
source.reproduced_from: Defense Centers for Public Health - Aberdeen (DCPH-A), 'Fluid Replacement & Work-Rest Guidelines to Prevent Heat Illness', TA-724-MAR23, and 'Heat Illness Prevention Guide', TA-010-MAR23
source.note: The 2003 edition had three work columns (Easy / Moderate / Hard). The 2022 edition has four (Easy / Moderate / Heavy / Very Heavy) and relaxed several Moderate cells to no-limit. 'Hard' is accepted here as an alias for 'Heavy'. Models that recall the 2003 card produce different cells (for example Moderate work in Heat Category 3 was 40/20, now NL).

units.work_min: minutes of work per hour; null with no_limit=true means NL (no limit)
units.rest_min: minutes of rest per hour; null when work is NL
units.max_work_min: continuous work duration in minutes; null with no_limit=true means NL

Easy.examples: weapons maintenance, marksmanship training, drill and ceremony

Moderate.examples: patrolling with a 30-pound load, low and high crawl, digging a defensive position

Heavy.examples: patrolling with a 45-pound load, 4-person litter carry (180 pounds), jogging 4 mph

Very Heavy.examples: 2-person litter carry (150 pounds), move under direct fire, obstacle course

work_rest_table.title: Table 1. Fluid Replacement and Work-Rest Guidelines for Training up to 4 Continuous Hours

continuous_work_table.title: Table 2. Recommendations for Continuous Work Duration and Fluid Replacement
continuous_work_table.note: Specific rest cycle durations are not prescribed for continuous operations; however, leaders should ensure rest breaks for Heat Category 3 and above.

notes: NL = no limit to work time per hour (Table 1) or to continuous work duration (Table 2).
Rest means minimal physical activity (sitting or standing), accomplished in shade if possible.
Do not exceed 1 quart per hour under most conditions; under very strenuous conditions a maximum of 1.5 quarts per hour or 12 quarts per day may be advised.
MOPP 4: add 10 F to the WBGT index for easy work and 20 F for moderate and hard work. Body armor: add 5 F to the WBGT index.
Table 1 applies to limited or controlled activities such as training up to 4 continuous hours; Table 2 applies to operations that may exceed 4 hours.
